content.text: Abscess b/n palatine tonsil & pharyngeal musc ← comp of tonsillitis or pharyngitis –
: often polymicrobial – group A strep (S. pyogenes) · staph aureus · resp anaerobes
Spontaneous (obstructed gland) or sequela of progressive tonsillitis
swollen or fluctuant tonsil → uvula deviation to
Abscess vs peritonsillar cellulitis: tonsillar swelling + uvula deviation = abscess
CT imaging of choice to differentiate b/n abscess & cellulitis
» premedicate opioid + intramucosal anesthetic - U/S guidance for area of fluctuance
» sheathed needle w 1cm exposed (⍉overshoot into internal carotid a.) - superior tonsillar pole (halfway b/n uvula & maxillary alveolar ridge) → middle → inferior pole until pus
» avoid internal carotid a. (2.5cm posterolat to tonsil) - Comp: carotid a. laceration
» well-appearing & tolerating fluids → d/c w PO Augmentin or clindamycin after drainage - ⍉clindamycin alone (requires drainage)
ENT consult ⍉needed for 1st peritonsillar abscess (EM scope) - recurr abscess/tonsillitis → outpt Refer for tonsillectomy
– reserved for pts who fail to respond to drainage · comp · recurr or severe
•deep neck space infect behind posterior pharyngeal wall
midline or unilat posterior pharyngeal wall edema (MC)
•anterior cervical LAD · lat neck mass or swelling
>50% width of adjacent vertebral body (XR in ext · C2 level · children <5yo)
w abx for lrg & mature abscesses in the OR
may be observed for 24-48hrs w antibiotic therapy
Bact: often polymicrobial - S. aureus MC · anaerobes · viridans group strep · Eikenella corrodens
⍉Infectious: sialolithiasis · EToH use dx · DM · uremia · drugs (anticholinergics · antihist) · malig

RF: age <1yr · older age · recent surg or intubation · dehydration · poor oral hygiene · eating dx (anorexia · bulimia) · sialoliths · neoplasms · Sjogren · HIV - bact rare in older children & adolescents
Comp: airway compromise · Lemierre syndrome (septic thrombophlebitis) · facial n. palsy · bacteremia · osteomyelitis
PE: unilat · firm · erythematous swelling of pre- & postauricular areas → extends to angle of mandible
Severe infect: fever · leukocytosis · significant comorbidity (IS) - degree of swelling → poss deep neck ext
Hydration · broad-spectrum ABX - cover staph ± MRSA if RF (prior MRSA · nursing home)
•moxifloxacin: IV · anti-staph & broad-spectrum - ⍉1st-line · CI in peds (tendinopathy)
